L134.en: The first degree is always red, whatever the key, and the chord’s shape doesn’t move: it’s like a capo on a guitar.

L135.en: Each note keeps the colour of its chakra, whatever the scale: Do is always red, Sol sky blue. A chord then becomes a blend, one colour per note.

L172.en: The interactive tools let you display your own handpan on screen, get immediate feedback on the notes you play […]

L173.en: “Having already used another app, I can say that this one is by far my favourite, it is so complete!”

L175.en: “I took my first steps on the handpan with David and today I’m continuing my learning with Constellations. Having already used another app, I can say that this one is by far my favourite, it is so complete!

L176.en: The more I use it, the more I realise how well it lives up to its name. It truly opens up the field of all possibilities!

L177.en: What I particularly appreciate is that it goes well beyond online lessons. The interactive tools let you display your own handpan on screen, get immediate feedback on the notes you play, choose a tempo or play along with a drum accompaniment. You also explore rhythm, singing, the expression of emotions and a multitude of scales. Plenty to learn, experiment and progress on your own!

L178.en: The platform also evolves regularly thanks to the ideas and needs of its users, and every improvement benefits everyone.

L179.en: And then there’s David! A passionate, kind teacher who listens, and who knows how to adapt his teaching to each person. In particular, he offered me different approaches to work on my difficulties with rhythm and supported me in using my electronic handpan with the app.

L180.en: A platform I recommend without hesitation, both to beginners and to experienced and professional musicians who want to enrich their practice and explore new musical possibilities!”

L181.en: Marina Fortuna · David’s student, electronic handpan · translated from French

L217.en: “The tool I wish I’d been taught as a child”

L218.en: I started the drums at 4, and music theory cut me off from wanting to play, so I learned by ear. At 12, at the piano, I realised my memory wasn’t built to decode abstract notes: it’s visual-motor and spatial. With the handpan I hit the same wall: spaceships with no pilot’s manual. So I drew. From those drawings came the tool I wish I’d been given: music theory made visible, in languages a child can understand.

L223.en: Do I need a digital pan?

L224.en: No. The app is designed first for your acoustic handpan, whatever it is. If you have a digital pan, you can connect that too.

L226.en: Everything you need to get to know your instrument and play: your scale, your chords, the library, singing to find your voice, playing technique, and saving what you create.

L227.en: What if I don’t know my scale?

L228.en: Play it into the mic and the app finds it.

L229.en: I’ve never learned to read music. Is it for me?

L230.en: Yes. You start with colours and emotions. Note names and theory come when you ask for them.

L231.en: Will I be asked for my card details?

L232.en: No. The free account doesn’t ask for a card, and it stays free with no time limit. You’ll only be asked for your card the day you choose a paid plan.

L234.en: Sign up, put your handpan in front of you and let the app listen to it. It takes care of the rest.
